findings.evidence: Protocol defines the new state slice and forbids prior slices and scientific artifacts as inputs (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:5,28-31); the contract preserves the no-prior-artifact boundary (contract.md:23-28), consistent with the supplied V2 terminal closure (123-plasticity-guard-independent-replication-v2-terminal-closure-2026-08-29.md:66-69).

The stated estimand is selection policy rather than update count (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:13-26). Both candidates are trained and evaluated in every arm and every arm commits six candidates (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:181-198); only the selection policy differs (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:207-226).

The protocol fixes the cached model path, runtime tuple, additive runner and validator paths, and external PrimaryED/DAed roots (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:48-89). The contract fixes model, runtime, and source manifest fields and rejects repository-internal or noncanonical roots (contract.md:63-88).

The protocol fixes 24 Gutenberg IDs, URLs, normalization, windows, and split lists (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:91-166), but the contract requires a corpus-manifest source_id field without defining its identity or relation to document_id (contract.md:90-96). The locked model tokenizer and tokenizer manifest are also named but no exact tokenizer file identity or tokenizer-manifest schema is declared (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:54-58,153-163; contract.md:90-96). Token-window and corpus identity are therefore not fully executable.

The protocol fixes eight seeds, two orders, six slots, canonical A/B pair windows, candidate seed derivation, LoRA and optimizer settings, byte-identical active-adapter starts, and immutable base-checkpoint semantics (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:170-205).

The three arms are explicitly defined and differ only in selection policy (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:207-226). The protocol and contract require 12 candidate trainings, 12 current evaluations, 12 protected evaluations, six commits, six rejected candidates, and equal counts across arms and cases (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:193-198; contract.md:150-167).

Primary and secondary contrasts, the 0.010 NLL/token threshold, strict win rule, 10/16 win requirement, deterministic 10,000-resample bootstrap seed and resampling algorithm, and no-rescue multiplicity rule are explicit (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:228-255).

The power preflight fixes replicate count, nominal normal mean and standard deviation, seed, and decision thresholds (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:257-266), but it does not specify the normal sampler or transformation and therefore does not define a reproducible 100,000-replicate stream. The reliability terms also leave stable selection logs and complete adapter files undefined (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:268-272).

Qualification requires an exact probe sequence length but declares no value or probe-token construction; the 128 maximum sequence length is only stated for candidate training (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:185-190,274-294). The qualification receipt records shapes but the contract does not supply the missing expected probe identity or exact shape contract (contract.md:98-103). This prevents independent execution of the qualification gates.

The lock key set and timing are specified (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:296-316), but configuration digest construction, inputs, canonicalization, and binding are not defined. The contract requires an exact configuration digest for assessment while the runner interface provides no configuration-digest argument or schema (contract.md:43-67); results merely names config_sha256 (contract.md:105-112). Prediction locking is therefore not fully enforceable.

The no-execution boundary is explicit before acceptance and before pre-assessment review (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:33-44,296-322), but the pre-assessment receipt has no exact top-level schema, unknown-key rule, receipt digest, file identity, or exact invocation contract. The contract lists required fields only (contract.md:145-148), while the packet additionally requires configuration-digest acceptance (134-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-review-packet.md:99-105).

The validator command and ten declared path arguments are bounded, and isolation/no-runner/no-model behavior is stated (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:324-345; contract.md:169-182). However, no exact schema or byte destination for the validator's one aggregate receipt is defined, and event payload/hash construction and the complete root-file input closure are not specified beyond field names (contract.md:114-143). Independent byte-level validation is consequently incomplete.

The protocol and contract prohibit raw evidence in aggregate output and keep raw artifacts external (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:347-354; contract.md:177-188). They do not define the separately recorded cleanup command, cleanup target manifest, or an executable credential/environment redaction and scrubbing procedure; the validator's clean environment does not establish runner or retained-artifact redaction (contract.md:38-41,169-182).

The classification enum, failure precedence, bounded meaning of DevelopmentNoCandidate, narrow candidate claim, and prohibitions on general improvement, benchmark, safety, production, Astral, Stage 0C, Stage 1, causal-self-modeling, and consciousness claims are explicit (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:356-377).

The exact runner interface permits only qualification, fit-tune, assessment, and full modes (contract.md:43-61), but the required pre-review verification command invokes an undeclared contract-check mode (contract.md:190-203). The full mode also depends on an unspecified implementation-authorized orchestration record (contract.md:56-61), leaving an authority gap in the implementation contract despite the stated provider/H100 prohibitions (133-plasticity-guard-equal-budget-mechanism-v1-protocol.md:39-44).
